title: Best Credit Cards for Award Travel in 2026

# Best Credit Cards for Award Travel in 2026


**Advertiser disclosure:** Pointhound earns a commission when you apply for some of the cards on this page. That compensation can affect which cards we feature and the order they appear in. It does not change what we say about them. We collect card details independently from issuer sites, and everything here is accurate as of August 14, 2026. Card terms change often, so confirm the details with the issuer before you apply. The "best for" labels, the ordering, and any credit score range on this page are guidance, not guarantees.


Most lists of the best credit card for flights rank cards on annual fee, welcome bonus size and lounge access. If your goal is a business class seat paid for with points, none of those three decides anything. What decides it is which airline loyalty programs the card's points can move into, because that is what determines the flights you can actually book.


You already know the transfer beats the portal. The hard part is that there are dozens of cards in front of you and no obvious way to tell which lead somewhere good and which lead to a booking screen where your points are worth a fixed cent and a half.


So this is nine cards for award travel, grouped by the five programs whose points transfer out to airlines. For each one: what it earns, which airlines it unlocks, and who it suits.


We can rank them this way because Pointhound searches award availability across 21 loyalty programs and 200+ airlines on 75,000+ routes. We see which programs have seats on a route, not just which ones have partners on paper.


## What Actually Makes a Credit Card Good for Award Travel?


A credit card is good for award travel when its points transfer to enough airline programs that no single airline's award availability can block your trip.


Four things decide it, in this order.


**1. The transfer partner network.** How many airline programs the card's points reach, and whether those programs fly your routes. Fourteen partners across five continents beats four, even if the four-partner card earns faster.


**2. The transfer ratio.** Whether 1,000 of your points become 1,000 airline miles or fewer. This is what issuers are least open about, and ratios move. Chase told cardholders in 2026 that its rate to one hotel partner would drop, and points everyone to the Ultimate Rewards portal for current rates ([Chase](https://creditcards.chase.com/business-credit-cards/ink/business-preferred) ). Capital One publishes its ratios openly ([Capital One](https://www.capitalone.com/learn-grow/money-management/venture-miles-transfer-partnerships/) ).


**3. The earn rate on what you already buy.** A card earning 4X at supermarkets is worth more than one earning 5X on a travel portal you never use.


**4. The annual fee against what you get back.** Not the headline value of the perk list. The value of the credits you will genuinely redeem.


Lounge access, elite status and hotel credits come last. They are nice. They are not what gets you the seat.


The big roundups optimize for something else: the dollar value of a benefits package, scored across seven generic axes, with transfer partners treated as a card category rather than a ranking axis. That is a fair way to rank a card you plan to spend on, and the wrong way to rank one you plan to fly on. It also skips the[gap between the credit card portal and a transfer](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/credit-card-portal-vs-transferring-points) , where points worth a fixed cent through the portal reach 2 to 20 times that in the right airline program, roughly 10 times in business class and up to 20 in first.


One thing to be clear about before the list: the ordering and the "best for" labels are editorial guidance, not a scored ranking. We do not give cards a number out of ten, because the right card depends on where you want to fly.

## Best Chase Cards for Award Travel: Sapphire Preferred and Sapphire Reserve


Chase Ultimate Rewards points transfer to ten airline programs covering North America, Europe and Asia, which makes the Sapphire cards a natural starting point for award travel.


[**Chase Sapphire Preferred**](https://www.pointhound.com/cards/chase-sapphire-preferred) carries a $95 annual fee and is currently offering 75,000 points after you spend $5,000 in the first three months. It earns 5X on Chase Travel, 3X on dining, 3X on gas stations, electric vehicle charging and vacation homes at top brands, 3X on top streaming services and online grocery, 2X on all other travel and 1X on everything else. Chase adds a $100 annual hotel credit through Chase Travel and up to $120 every four years toward Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS ([Chase](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred) ).


[**Chase Sapphire Reserve**](https://www.pointhound.com/cards/chase-sapphire-reserve) is the premium version at $795, plus $195 for each authorized user. The current offer is 100,000 points after $6,000 in the first three months. It earns 8X on Chase Travel, 4X on flights and hotels booked direct, 3X on dining worldwide and 1X on everything else, and it carries a $300 annual travel credit plus access to Chase Sapphire Lounges and more than 1,300 Priority Pass lounges with up to two guests ([Chase](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve) ).


Both cards feed the same ten airline programs: Aer Lingus AerClub, Air Canada Aeroplan, British Airways, Flying Blue for Air France and KLM, Iberia Plus, JetBlue TrueBlue, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, Southwest Rapid Rewards, United MileagePlus and Virgin Atlantic Flying Club.


What that buys you is transatlantic depth. Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic and Iberia all price Europe differently on the same day, so having three is worth more than having one. Aeroplan reaches past Air Canada to the wider group of airlines it shares partners with, including United, Lufthansa and Singapore Airlines, and that is what opens Asia.


Where the Preferred falls short: ten partners is a solid network, not the widest, and Chase has no partner in the Middle East or South America. The Reserve has a different problem. **$795 is a lot of card.** It works if you will use the $300 credit and the lounges, and it does not if you fly twice a year.


For redeeming inside the program once you have the points, see the full[Chase Ultimate Rewards playbook](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/chase-ultimate-rewards-how-to-use-your-points-for-maximum-flight-value) .


## Best Amex Cards for Award Travel: Gold and Platinum


American Express Membership Rewards reaches a broad set of international airline programs, which is why Amex points open premium cabins the other four issuers cannot.


[**American Express Gold**](https://www.pointhound.com/cards/amex-gold) has a $325 annual fee. Amex advertises a welcome offer as high as 100,000 Membership Rewards points after $8,000 in purchases in the first six months, and says plainly that offers vary and you may not be eligible for one. It earns 4X at restaurants worldwide on up to $50,000 per calendar year, 4X at U.S. supermarkets on up to $25,000 per year, 5X on prepaid hotels through Amex Travel, 3X on flights booked through Amex Travel or directly with the airline, and 1X on everything else. The credits are food-shaped: $120 dining, $120 Uber Cash, $100 Resy and $84 Dunkin', all requiring enrollment ([American Express](https://www.americanexpress.com/us/credit-cards/card/gold-card/) ).


[**American Express Platinum**](https://www.pointhound.com/cards/amex-platinum) is $895, with an advertised offer as high as 175,000 points after $12,000 in the first six months and the same caveat that offers vary by applicant. It earns 5X on flights booked directly with airlines or through Amex Travel on up to $500,000 per calendar year, and 5X on prepaid hotels through Amex Travel. The benefits are airport-shaped: more than 1,550 lounges through the Global Lounge Collection, a $600 hotel credit, a $200 airline fee credit, a $219 CLEAR Plus credit and a $120 Uber One credit ([American Express](https://www.americanexpress.com/us/credit-cards/card/platinum/) ).


One limitation before you apply. Amex says on both card pages that points transfer to 20 airline and hotel travel partners, but it does not publish an airline-only count or a public ratio table the way Capital One does, and not every Amex partner transfers at 1:1. Most transfers land instantly, though some take up to five days, which matters when the seat you found is one of two left.


The Gold's credits are worth real money only if you eat where Amex wants you to eat. The Platinum carries the highest fee here and earns 1X on ordinary spending, so treat it as a benefits card that happens to earn points rather than an earning card.


For the redemption side, see our guide to[getting the most from Amex Membership Rewards](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/amex-membership-rewards-how-to-get-the-most-value) .


## Best Capital One Cards for Award Travel: Venture and Venture X


Capital One miles reach 18 airline programs, more than any other issuer publishes openly, and the Venture cards earn a flat rate on every purchase.


That flat rate suits anyone who will not track spending categories.


[**Capital One Venture Rewards**](https://www.pointhound.com/cards/capital-one-venture) costs $95 a year and is offering 75,000 bonus miles after $4,000 in purchases in the first three months. It earns unlimited 2X miles on every purchase and 5X on hotels, vacation rentals and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel, plus up to $120 toward Global Entry or TSA PreCheck ([Capital One](https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/venture/) ).


[**Capital One Venture X**](https://www.pointhound.com/cards/capital-one-venture-x-rewards) costs $395 and carries the same 75,000-mile offer after $4,000 in three months. It earns 10X on hotels and rental cars and 5X on flights and vacation rentals through Capital One Travel, 2X on everything else, plus 10,000 bonus miles every year from your first anniversary, a $300 annual Capital One Travel credit and access to Capital One Lounges and 1,300 or more Priority Pass lounges ([Capital One](https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/venture-x/) ).


The partner list is where Capital One earns its place, and it is the only complete airline list with ratios you can check without logging in. Fourteen airline programs transfer at 1:1: Aeromexico, Air Canada Aeroplan, Avianca LifeMiles, British Airways, Cathay Pacific Asia Miles, Etihad Guest, Finnair Plus, Flying Blue, Qantas, Qatar Airways Privilege Club, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, TAP Miles and Go, Turkish Airlines Miles and Smiles, and Virgin Red. Three transfer at 2:1.5, meaning 1,000 miles become 750: Emirates Skywards, EVA Air and Japan Airlines. JetBlue transfers at 5:3. The minimum transfer is 1,000 miles ([Capital One](https://www.capitalone.com/learn-grow/money-management/venture-miles-transfer-partnerships/) ).


Qatar, Etihad, Turkish and Avianca are the names to notice. They reach the Middle East, Africa and South America, and they are why a Capital One balance books premium cabins a Chase balance cannot.


Two things to weigh against that. Flat-rate 2X is simple, but if much of your spending is dining and groceries you will earn slower here than on a category card. And **four of the eighteen partners transfer at worse than 1:1** , so read the ratio before you move anything.


Our[Capital One Venture miles guide](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/capital-one-venture-miles-maximize-value-for-flights) covers the redemption side.


## Best Citi Card for Award Travel: Strata Premier


Citi ThankYou points reach American Airlines, which Chase and Capital One do not, making the Strata Premier a strong second card rather than a first.


The card costs $95 a year and is offering 60,000 bonus ThankYou points after $4,000 in spending in the first three months. It earns 10X on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Citi Travel, 3X on air travel, other hotel purchases, restaurants, supermarkets, and gas and electric vehicle charging stations, and 1X on everything else. There is a $100 annual hotel benefit and no foreign transaction fees ([Citi](https://www.citi.com/credit-cards/citi-strata-premier-credit-card) ).


On partners, Citi is the least forthcoming of the five. It names American Airlines, JetBlue, Virgin Atlantic, Cathay and EVA Air on the card page, then says "and others" without publishing the list or the ratios. The minimum transfer is 1,000 points.


American Airlines is the reason to hold this card. It is the one major U.S. carrier that neither Chase nor Capital One lists as a partner, so Citi points are how you book American without holding a co-branded American card. Add the Strata Premier second, once you know an American route matters to you.


## Best Bilt Card for Award Travel


Bilt earns transferable points on rent and mortgage payments, with no transaction fee on either, and every one of its travel partners transfers at 1:1.


The **Bilt Blue Card** has no annual fee. It earns up to 4X at more than 20,000 Bilt partner restaurants, 3X on hotels and 2X on flights booked through the Bilt travel portal, 3X on Lyft once you link the accounts, and 1X on everything else. On housing, it earns up to 1.25X on rent and mortgage payments when you select housing-only rewards, with no transaction fee and no cap on the payment amount. Bilt lists 28 airline and hotel transfer partners in total and says all travel partners transfer at 1:1. New cardholders get $100 of Bilt Cash rather than a points bonus ([Bilt](https://www.bilt.com/card) ).


The award-travel reason to care is that ratio. No other program here claims 1:1 across the board: Capital One has four partners below it, and Chase and Amex do not publish theirs. A clean 1:1 balance is what makes the math on a premium cabin work, as our guide to[flying first class with points](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/how-to-fly-first-class-with-points) shows. Bilt does not publish which airlines it reaches, so check the list in the app before you count on a program.


The earning mechanics have real conditions attached, and this is the section to read twice. Your housing multiplier depends on which rewards option you select and how much you spend elsewhere on the card, and Bilt Cash expires each December 31 with only $100 carrying over. Check the terms on Bilt's page before you assume a number. Bilt also sells the Obsidian at $95 a year and the Palladium at $495.


## Best Business Card for Award Travel: Ink Business Preferred


Business cards earn into the same transferable programs as personal cards, so freelance or side-business income can build an award balance without adding a new points currency.


[**Chase Ink Business Preferred**](https://www.pointhound.com/cards/ink-business-preferred) costs $95 a year and is offering 100,000 bonus points after $8,000 in purchases in the first three months. It earns 3X on the first $150,000 in combined annual spending across shipping, social media and search engine advertising, travel, and internet, cable and phone services, then 1X after that and on everything else. There are no foreign transaction fees ([Chase](https://creditcards.chase.com/business-credit-cards/ink/business-preferred) ).


The points are Chase Ultimate Rewards, the same currency the Sapphire cards earn, reaching the same ten airline programs. Hold both and the balances work together.


One condition: this only applies if you genuinely have business income. Do not invent a business to chase a bonus. If you have one, the 3X advertising category alone tends to out-earn most personal cards.


## Should You Get an Airline Credit Card Instead?


An airline credit card earns miles in one program only, which makes it a good second card once you know your airline and a poor first card.


The trade runs in both directions. A co-branded card brings things transferable points cannot: a free checked bag, priority boarding, sometimes better award pricing on that airline. If you fly United out of Denver forty times a year, a United card is not a mistake.


What it costs you is optionality. Your miles live in one program, and that program's award availability is the only availability you have. On the day you want to fly to Rome, if that airline has nothing, you have nothing. A transferable balance lets you check ten programs, find the one with a seat, and move the points then.


This is the most common way people end up disappointed with award travel. They earn 80,000 miles in one program, go to book, and find the seats are not there at the price they expected. The[CFPB found](https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_credit-card-rewards_issue-spotlight_2024-05.pdf) that travel providers have a long history of requiring more miles over time for the same trip, and that many programs now price in ways that make the cost hard to forecast.


Get the co-brand card second, after you know your airline. Pointhound has guide pages for co-branded cards too, including the[United Explorer](https://www.pointhound.com/cards/united-explorer) .


## How to Choose Your First Award Travel Credit Card


Pick the card whose transfer partners fly the route you actually want, check that its earn rate matches how you already spend, and compare annual fees last.


1. **Name the trip.** Not "somewhere in Europe." A specific route, in a specific month, in a specific cabin. Everything else follows from this.
2. **Find which programs book that route and what it costs in points.** This is where[Pointhound](https://www.pointhound.com/) belongs. We search award availability across 21 loyalty programs and 200+ airlines and return step-by-step booking instructions, so you see what your trip costs in points before you commit to a card. Search is free and no card is required.
3. **Work backwards to the cards that feed those programs.** If the seat is on Qatar, you need Capital One miles. If it is on American, Citi. If it is on United or Air France, Chase works. The route picks the card, not the other way around.
4. **Check the earn rate against your real spending.** Pull up last month's statement. Mostly groceries and restaurants, and the Amex Gold earns faster. Spread evenly with no pattern, and flat-rate 2X on the Venture wins.
5. **Apply, hit the welcome bonus honestly, then search before you transfer.** Transfers are one way and cannot be reversed. Confirm the award seat is live, transfer the exact number of points, and book immediately. Most transfers are instant; some Amex partners take up to five days, and a seat can disappear in five days.


The[full card comparison tool](https://www.pointhound.com/cards) covers 76+ cards with filters for issuer, annual fee and bonus categories. New to all of this? Start with[how to book flights with credit card points](https://www.pointhound.com/blog/how-to-book-flights-with-credit-card-points) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best credit card for booking flights with points?


The one whose transfer partners fly your route. For most beginners that means a card earning Chase Ultimate Rewards, Amex Membership Rewards or Capital One miles, because all three reach multiple airline programs rather than locking you to a single airline's award availability.


### How many credit cards do you need for award travel?


One is enough to start. A single card earning transferable points into a broad partner network will book real award flights. A second card usually earns its place only when it reaches airline programs the first one cannot, or transfers at a better ratio.


### Is an annual fee worth it for a travel credit card?


It depends on what you get back and how much you fly. Compare the fee against the credits and the earn rate you will genuinely use, not against the headline perk list. A low-fee card that transfers to good airline programs beats an expensive card whose credits you never redeem.


### Do you earn miles when you book an award flight?


Award bookings can sometimes earn miles. Some programs credit miles on award tickets and others do not, so check the rules of the specific program you are booking through. Either way, the value of the redemption comes from the discount against the cash fare.


### Should I transfer my points before I find a flight?


No. Transfers cannot be reversed, so confirm the award seat is available first, then transfer the exact number of points and book immediately. Most transfers are instant, but some Amex partners can take up to five days, and availability changes fast.


## Key Takeaways


- The deciding factor for an award travel card is its transfer partner network, not its annual fee, welcome bonus or lounge access.
- Points redeemed through a credit card portal return a low fixed rate. Transferred to the right airline program they reach 2 to 20 times that, roughly 10 times in business class and up to 20 in first.
- Chase, Amex, Capital One, Citi and Bilt are the five programs whose points transfer out to airlines. Each reaches a different set, and that difference decides which flights you can book.
- Capital One publishes 18 airline partners and their ratios. Chase publishes 10 partners but not its ratios. Amex, Citi and Bilt publish combined or partial lists, so check before you count on a number.
- Airline co-brand cards are a good second card once you know your airline, and a poor first card when you do not.
- Card terms change constantly. Confirm every fee, bonus and ratio on the issuer's own page before you apply.
- Find the seat before you transfer. Transfers are one way.


The right card is not the one with the biggest welcome bonus. It is the one whose points reach the airline that flies where you want to go, on the day you want to go there.
